name: e_getitem
reason: tcGetitem .e is halfToDouble, which mirrors PyFloat_Unpack2 (Objects/floatobject.c:2090-2143: infinity, NaN with its 10 fraction bits at :2118-2124, subnormal f/1024 * 2**-14, normal); ArrayFloatRoundTrip checks all 65536 patterns by kernel decide (HalfTrip.lean, 8 chunks) and says a[i] = a[i] gives the same pattern except the quiet bit of a signalling NaN, which matches 3.15.2 on every pattern (rerun: 0 mismatches). The round trip pins the read value only to within the rounding interval of each half; the difftest pins the exact double.

name: e_setitem
reason: tcSetitem .e follows the body in order: PyArg_Parse "f" (asDouble, then doubleToFloat), CHECK_ARRAY_BOUNDS, then PyFloat_Pack2 of the promoted float (packHalf mirrors floatobject.c:1895-2000, including both Overflow exits and the NaN mask at :1914-1925). ArrayFloatConv (re-checked after the fix; its new conjunct concerns Zf and Zd only) pins the two roundings, the conversion error before the index check, and the IndexError before Pack2 when idxOk is false. ArrayHalfStruct is refuted by the double rounding at 1 + 2**-11 + 2**-40, which reproduces on 3.15.2. The i < 0 branch, which skips Pack2, is covered by the refuted sequences-array-ins1-atomic.

name: f_getitem
reason: floatToDouble is the C (double) widening, which quiets a signalling NaN (fraction | 2**22, then << 29), and is not PyFloat_Unpack4, which unpack4 models separately; the round trip is proven for all 2**32 patterns by exponent class (fTrip). ArrayFloatItems is refuted by 0x7f800001 -> 0x7fc00001. Both reproduce on 3.15.2 and on main, where f_getitem still casts.

name: f_setitem
reason: tcSetitem .f is (float)PyFloat_AsDouble(v) (getargs.c:922-930), then CHECK_ARRAY_BOUNDS, then the store; doubleToFloat rounds to nearest even with the overflow to inf and the NaN truncation that the hardware cast does. ArrayFloatConv pins the composition and both orders of failure. ArraySingleStruct is refuted by 1e300 (inf where struct raises; rerun on 3.15.2), and quiet32 in the round trip states the signalling-NaN change.

name: d_getitem
reason: One-line body: PyFloat_FromDouble of the stored double, modelled as the pattern itself. The property that holds the row up is the round trip of ArrayFloatRoundTrip: every 64-bit pattern, signalling NaNs included, reads and stores back bit-exact, in contrast to f. That was checked against 3.15.2 for a signalling NaN.

name: d_setitem
reason: tcSetitem .d is PyArg_Parse "d" (asDouble), CHECK_ARRAY_BOUNDS, then the store. asDouble mirrors PyFloat_AsDouble (floatobject.c:246-303) branch by branch: float or subclass, nb_float with the exact, subclass+DeprecationWarning and TypeError result checks, the nb_index fallback through _PyNumber_Index and PyLong_AsDouble, and TypeError. ArrayFloatConv pins that order, the error before the bounds check, and the IndexError for idxOk false.

name: cf_getitem
reason: Each float part is widened by floatToDouble, as PyComplex_FromDoubles(f[0], f[1]) does implicitly, real part in the low word. The round trip gives quiet32 of each part, which matches 3.15.2 for a pair of signalling NaNs (0100c07f0200c0ff).

name: cf_setitem
reason: tcSetitem .Zf mirrors :693-710 in order: PyArg_Parse "D" (asComplex, PyComplex_AsCComplex at Objects/complexobject.c:545-570, the getargs.c:942-951 PyErr_Occurred check), CHECK_ARRAY_BOUNDS (:702), then (float) of each part, real part in the low word. ArrayFloatConv now pins all three steps: the value conjunct (doubleToFloat of each part), the conversion error raised for idxOk true and false (so a bounds check moved before the conversion fails it), and the new conjunct that a successful conversion with idxOk false raises IndexError (so a body without the re-check fails it). The idxOk flag standing for a conversion that shrank the array is the stated scope, as for e, f and d.

name: cd_getitem
reason: The two doubles are taken as stored (real part in the low 64 bits) and PyComplex_FromDoubles keeps them. The Zd round trip is bit-exact for every 128-bit pattern, signalling NaNs included, which matches 3.15.2.

name: cd_setitem
reason: tcSetitem .Zd mirrors :722-739: PyArg_Parse "D" via asComplex, CHECK_ARRAY_BOUNDS (:731), then the two doubles stored as is (real part in the low 64 bits). ArrayFloatConv pins the stored pattern, the conversion error before the bounds check for both idxOk values, and now the IndexError after a successful conversion when idxOk is false, so neither a missing re-check nor a check before the conversion satisfies it; the Zd round trip is bit-exact.

name: array_richcompare
reason: arrRich follows :918-1014: the NotImplemented check, the length shortcut for EQ/NE, the compareitems fast path for the same descriptor (b..Q, u signed wchar_t, w Py_UCS4), the item loop with getarrayitem errors propagating, compare_sizes, and the final PyObject_RichCompare. Bool is sound because the items are builtin int, float, complex or str. ArrayRichcompare proves that the fast path equals list_richcompare_impl (listobject.c:3459-3519, cited correctly) on the decoded items for every operator and typecode pair, and that raw C order holds for undecodable u/w items; a fast path with the wrong signedness or a missing shortcut would fail it. Spot checks on 3.15.2 agree: signed u, unsigned w, NaN unequal, -0.0 == 0.0, complex unordered.

name: array_array_fromfile_impl
reason: The fix separates PyBytes_GET_SIZE (:1776) from the buffer and now covers a raising __buffer__, item size != 1 and the ValueError (citations, including clinic/arraymodule.c.h:537-540, are right), but the bytesSub branch still omits the other Python callback on that buffer: PyBuffer_Release in frombytes (:1945, and :1919/1925/1935/1939 on its error paths) calls the subclass's __release_buffer__ (Objects/typeobject.c:11375-11399, 11516-11590) after the memcpy and before the EOFError test, and it can mutate the array. So ArrayFromFileSub's last conjunct (a2.items = a1.items ++ decodedItems) is proven but false on 3.15.2 and main: with a = array('b') and read returning an instance of class B(bytes) whose __release_buffer__ runs del a[:], a.fromfile(f, 2) leaves [] (the theorem says [1, 2]), and with a.append(9) there it leaves [1, 2, 9]. Model __release_buffer__ as a callback that may change the array (or say why it is out of scope); the rest (clinic n, MemoryError before read, read and non-bytes errors, ValueError before EOFError, the != test, BufferError, the ArrayFromFileDoc refutation) mirrors the body.

name: array_array_tofile_impl
reason: toFileLoop computes nbytes/nblocks once, skips an empty array, re-reads ob_item at each block (blockOf on the current array, cUB past its items), and stops at the first write that raises. ArrayToFile pins the 64 KiB blocks, one call each, in order, stopping at the failing call, with tobytes as their concatenation, for every non-mutating write. ArrayToFileSafe is refuted by a clearing write (SIGSEGV on 3.15.2 and main, a duplicate of the open #142884). A write that shrinks within the allocation is reported as cUB though C reads stale bytes there; that is conservative and does not affect the refutation.

name: array_repr

Both entries are refutations of the Doc/library/array.rst:298-312 eval promise that run this body: ArrayReprNames by array('Zd', [infj]) and ArrayReprWInjective by the dropped U+FEFF. Both reproduce on 3.15.2.
